headline: Chip and memory stocks suffered a second day of heavy selling, wiping more than $1 trillion off the value of the biggest names this week.
score_reason: Large, multi-market chip sell-off with figures from Business Insider; facts support the pool score.
importance_line: Chip shares and the AI spending behind them are under pressure from inflation, rate-hike bets and debt worries, which affects fund and pension holders as well as chip makers and AI borrowers, but analysts disagree on whether the drop is ending.
summary: Business Insider reports that the largest chip and memory companies have lost more than $1 trillion in market value this week, leaving the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index, a benchmark of US chip stocks, 12% below its early-October peak. The selling began in South Korea and spread after Chinese chip firm CXMT said it had advanced a denser memory design, while hotter US inflation data and worries about AI companies' borrowing added to it; JPMorgan strategists suggested the rout may be nearing an end.
